Telefônica Brasil S.A. (VIV) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
sum: Telefônica Brasil S.A., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a mobile telecommunications company in Brazil. Its fixed line voice services portfolio includes local, domestic long-distance, and international long-distance calls; and mobile portfolio comprises voice and broadband internet access through 3G, 4G, 4.5G, and 5G, as well as value-added, prepaid plans with data sharing features, family plans, voice mail, caller identification, voice minutes in unlimited bundles to mobile and fixed-line phones, and digital services, and wireless roaming services. The company also offers data services, including broadband and mobile data services; fixed-line local services consist of activation, monthly subscription, public telephones and measured services. In addition, it provides pay TV services through IPTV technologies; network services, such as rental of facilities and other services; wholesale services, including interconnection services to users of other network providers; and digital services that include entertainment, cloud, and security and financial services. Further, the company offers multimedia communication services, which include audio, data, voice and other sounds, images, texts, and other information, as well as sells devices and accessories, such as smartphones, broadband USB modems, and other devices. Additionally, it provides telecommunications solutions and IT support to various industries, such as retail, manufacturing, services, financial institutions, government, etc; insurance services; and sale of wireless devices and consumer electronics. It markets and sells its solutions through Vivo stores, dealers, retail channels, distribution and digital channels, door-to-door sales, and outbound tele sales. The company was formerly known as Telecomunicações de São Paulo S.A. - TELESP and changed its name to Telefônica Brasil S.A. in October 2011. Telefônica Brasil S.A. was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in São Paulo, Brazil.

America Movil stock weighs mobile growth against forecast miss
sum: America Movil reported stronger third-quarter operating performance on October 20, 2026, but its results fell short of analyst expectations. In a Reuters report carried by Fidelity, the Mexican telecommunications group posted net profit of 24.28 billion Mexican pesos, up 7 percent from the year-earlier quarter. Revenue increased 7.6 percent to 250.63 billion Mexican pesos.

The earnings growth was not enough to meet the forecasts compiled by LSEG. Analysts had expected dollar-denominated net profit of 1.51 billion dollars and revenue of 14.05 billion dollars, compared with the reported figures of 1.34 billion dollars and 13.86 billion dollars respectively.

Fixed broadband added another growth pillar. The group connected 390,000 new broadband accesses during the quarter, with Brazil, Colombia and Argentina among the main contributors. The combination of postpaid growth and broadband additions supports revenue quality, although the forecast miss leaves investors focused on the pace at which operating gains translate into earnings.

America Movil completed its acquisition of Brazilian broadband provider Desktop in early October. The transaction expands the group's presence in a market where postpaid and fixed-line demand were already important contributors to the quarter. It also gives the company an additional route to bundle mobile and broadband services.

The broader competitive backdrop is becoming more demanding. Televisa is moving ahead with its acquisition of AT&T's Mexico unit, a transaction that could create a larger rival in Mexico's telecommunications market. For America Movil, the development raises the importance of customer retention, network investment and disciplined integration of the Desktop business.

America Movil stock traded at 23.00 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:35 CET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The quote provides a current trading reference, while the earnings miss and the completed Brazilian acquisition remain the central factors for investors assessing the shares.
The broader US equity market remains the relevant market frame for investors following S&P 500 developments alongside company-specific results.

Proximus (ENXTBR:PROX), Why Is It Back In The Spotlight?
sum: Proximus (ENXTBR:PROX) is back under the spotlight after third quarter and nine month earnings showed softer sales and revenue, but a higher quarterly net profit and earnings per share from continuing operations.

Recent trading suggests a short burst of optimism around Proximus. The share price is up 9.71% over the past month and 4.03% over the last week, yet year to date it remains down 11.47% and the 5 year total shareholder return has fallen 45.70%. This points to momentum that is improving in the short term but weak over a longer horizon as investors reassess the balance between earnings resilience and ongoing risks.
Spot similar rebounds and pressure points by scanning our hand picked 227 high quality undervalued stocks, featuring balance sheets and cash flows that may support earnings resilience.

For a stock like Proximus that has already bounced on a better quarterly profit but still shows a weak multi year return, the real tension now sits in the valuation. Is most of the potential recovery already in the price, or not yet?

On the Simply Wall St analyst consensus Narrative, Proximus screens as undervalued, with a fair value of €7.92 versus the last close at €6.33. That framework blends analyst earnings forecasts, margin assumptions and a 9.45% discount rate into a single valuation anchor.

Full ownership of Unifiber and intended fiber cooperation agreements in Flanders and Wallonia are designed to reduce long term network access costs, refinance Unifiber’s approximately €400 million of bank debt at group rates, and shift more customers onto owned or co owned infrastructure, which may improve domestic EBITDA and organic free cash flow.
Still, Proximus faces real pressure if high fibre CapEx drags on free cash flow or if fierce Belgian competition pushes more customers into lower priced brands.

Millicom Stock Revenue Beat Raises Margin Questions After Q3 Earnings
sum: Millicom International Cellular reported Q3 2026 sales of US$2,276 million and net income of US$98 million, with earnings per share of US$0.58 from continuing operations, while reaffirming full year equity free cash flow guidance of around US$1.1 billion and a leverage goal below 2.5x.

Management highlighted progress on its Double E and more for more plans, including significant postpaid migration from the prepaid base and stronger convergence. This helped deliver US$2.28 billion in quarterly revenue that exceeded some analyst expectations, even as earnings per share fell short of consensus forecasts.
The next area of focus will be how Millicom’s revenue outperformance, alongside an earnings miss, may reshape the broader investment narrative.

To own Millicom International Cellular, you need to buy into a Latin American telecom story built on postpaid upgrades, convergence and disciplined cash generation. The latest quarter still leans into that idea. Service revenue was solid, equity free cash flow guidance of about US$1.1b was reaffirmed and the leverage goal below 2.5x stayed intact.

The short term swing factor is whether earnings pressure eases while debt keeps trending lower. Q3 net income and EPS were weaker than a year ago, so any delay in margin recovery or higher interest costs remains the biggest operational risk. On this front, the earnings miss looks important, not noise.

The most relevant update alongside the earnings print is management’s confirmation that Millicom International Cellular is on track for roughly US$1.1b in equity free cash flow in 2026 while targeting leverage below 2.5x. For a business carrying about US$8.1b of net debt, that cash profile sits at the center of the thesis.

That same announcement underlined execution on the Double E and more for more plans, with 73% of postpaid sales coming from the prepaid base and strong take up of convergent offers. For you, the key question is whether this operational mix shift offsets margin pressure and refinancing risk quickly enough to keep that cash flow target credible.

items.t: Buy, Sell, or Hold? Tuesday's Top Upgrades and Downgrades: AON, Bloom Energy, Chevron, Cloudflare, Marvell Technologies, Lumentum Holdings, Merck & Co., Roku, X-Energy, and More
sum: Tech stocks keep beating estimates and then selling off anyway, Apple just joined the club, and Wall Street analysts are busy reshuffling their ratings on everything from nuclear energy plays to insurance giants. Here is who got upgraded, downgraded, and…

Futures are trading mixed early Tuesday, with the Dow Futures down 300 points after yet another tech titan posted outstanding numbers that beat Wall Street estimates, then, like clockwork, sold off in the aftermarket. This time, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL | AAPL Price Prediction) was the victim; while it was torpedoed after the results were posted, it was still down less than some other mega-cap technology stocks that reported over the last 10 days. iPhone sales were outstanding as demand for the iPhone 18 surged, while service revenue hit an all-time high of $31.57 billion. Reasons for the post-earnings sell-off ranged from the company missing revenue estimates for China to rising costs for memory chips, which are starting to pressure gross margins, which the company lowered for the December quarter. The bottom line is the tech sell-off and investor rotation likely still have a way to go.

After a solid start to the trading week, stocks rolled over after the noon hour, and the same reasons stayed front and center. Massive AI spending and worries about big tech stocks’ lack of free cash flow, which in the past had never been an issue, and concerns over the potential for the Democrats to regain the House of Representatives are all contributing to a quiet market sell-off, and with the October jobs report this Friday and the inflation reports next week all still on the burner, those data points will have the ability to move the market.

Three of the four major indices closed lower Monday, with only the Dow Jones Industrials closing higher at 51,938, up 0.41%, while the Nasdaq was the big loser Monday, closing at 25,164, down 1.07%. The S&P 500 ended the session at 7,541, down 0.51%, and the small-cap Russell 2000 closed at 2,805, down 0.21%.

Desktop stock: Claro NXT completes 72.83% acquisition
sum: Claro NXT, a subsidiary of América Móvil, completed the acquisition of a controlling stake in Desktop on October 1, 2026. In its Form 6-K, América Móvil said its Brazilian subsidiary acquired 72.83% of Desktop's capital stock.

The deal transfers control of the Brazilian telecommunications provider to Claro NXT. Telecompaper reported that Claro NXT intends to submit a request to Brazil's securities regulator for a unified tender offer for the remaining shares.

The proposed process is also intended to facilitate a change in Desktop's issuer registration from Category A to Category B. For minority shareholders, the next key developments are the tender-offer terms and the regulatory process that follows the change of control.

Desktop is a Brazilian telecommunications provider focused on internet and connectivity services. Its operations are now being integrated into Claro NXT's fixed broadband platform, giving América Móvil a larger regional infrastructure and customer base in Brazil. The ownership change places Desktop within the expansion of Claro's fixed-network business rather than leaving it as an independent listed operator.
Brazil's broader equity market can be followed through the Bovespa index.

For investors, the tender offer and any subsequent changes to Desktop's listing status are more immediate issues than operating results. The final terms and regulatory filings will determine the options available to remaining shareholders.

America Movil SAB de CV Stock (AMX) Moved Up by 5.46% on Oct 21: A Full Analysis
sum: America Movil SAB de CV (AMX) moved up by 5.46%. The Telecommunications Services sector is up by 3.59%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: SpaceX (SPCX) up 6.42%; AT&T Inc (T) down 6.23%; Verizon Communications Inc (VZ) down 2.37%.

América Móvil registered a strong upward rally during today's trading session, driven primarily by investor enthusiasm following the release of its third-quarter financial results. The Latin American telecommunications giant delivered top-line revenue growth that surpassed consensus Wall Street expectations, bolstered by resilient consumer demand across its core geographic segments. A sharp expansion in postpaid mobile subscribers across key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and Colombia served as a primary growth driver, reinforcing the company's leading market share and pricing power across the region.

Beyond top-line momentum, operational efficiency and profitability metrics provided strong support for the stock's positive price action. EBITDA grew at a faster pace than overall service revenue, demonstrating improved margin performance and tight cost discipline across network operations. Free cash flow generation experienced significant year-over-year acceleration, providing management with amplified flexibility to fully fund cash flows while maintaining active share buyback programs and dividend distributions. Furthermore, continued progress in balance sheet leverage reduction strengthened institutional confidence in the firm's long-term capital structure.

Market sentiment was further bolstered during the management conference call, where executives highlighted stable demand trends, competitive advantages in 5G deployment, and disciplined capital allocation. Analysts responded favorably to the company's ongoing strategic transition toward enhanced capital return yields following recent tactical consolidation in regional markets. The combination of better-than-expected revenue, expanding operating margins, robust cash generation, and reassuring forward guidance prompted widespread institutional buying, pushing the stock sharply higher with elevated trading activity.

items.t: SBA goes all-in on Central America with 600 towers planned for 2026
sum: SBA Communications plans to build about 600 towers in 2026, most of them in Central America, as the US tower operator expands its international footprint to serve Millicom and other regional carriers.

International builds accelerated in the second quarter, with 99 new towers completed compared to 75 in the first quarter, and the company expects the pace to increase in each successive quarter this year.

"In the second quarter, we saw increased new tower construction as we ramped up efforts in Central America building sites for Millicom and others," CEO Brendan Cavanagh said during the earnings results release.

SBA owned 10,948 sites in the region at the end of the second quarter, up from 10,905 in the first quarter, while its global portfolio grew to 46,390 sites from 46,358. South America, by contrast, edged down slightly to 14,326 sites from 14,347 over the same period.

The customer base behind SBA's international revenue also shifted. Millicom's Tigo share of international site leasing revenue jumped to 19.6% in the second quarter from 6.7% a year earlier, while Telefónica's share fell to 18.7% from 21.8%. América Móvil eased to 19.4% from 19.8%, and TIM slipped to 12.2% from 14.0%.

Asked on the earnings call about tower rents in Latin America, Cavanagh said the dynamic there is not fundamentally different from SBA's other markets, since all customers are looking for ways to control costs, including their rents.

"It's really a matter of making sure that what we're delivering to them is of greater value than the costs that they're incurring in order to be there," he said, adding that high-quality locations and responsive service and support help the company retain tenants. Cases where a customer drops a site because it is no longer needed or a cheaper alternative exists do happen, he said, but are "more the exception than the rule."

Telefónica agrees deal to sell Mexican unit for $450m
sum: Telefónica has agreed a deal to sell its Mexican unit to Melisa Acquisition LLC for $450 million.
The deal was confirmed by the Spanish telco in a stock market statement this week, with the carrier noting the transaction is in line with its plans to slim down its Latin American footprint.
Telefónica has been looking to sell its Mexican unit for some time, with previous reports suggesting the telco was in talks with Beyond ONE, the owner of Virgin Mobile Mexico, over a sale last year.
Melisa Acquisition is a consortium of investors led by Oxio and Newfoundland Capital Management.
The carrier, which operates under the Movistar brand, is the second-biggest telco in Mexico, with more than 25 million customers.

During its time in Mexico, Telefónica has struggled to gain market share from Carlos Slim’s dominant carrier in the country, America Movil SAB. Indeed, the telco isn't the only carrier to push for an exit, with AT&T Mexico also heavily focused on finalizing an exit.
Telefónica's planned Mexican sale is subject to regulatory approval. For now, the market is one of the few Latin American markets that the carrier still operates in, along with Brazil and Venezuela.

items.t: Streaming Media Services Market Size, Share & Forecast to 2036
sum: In 2025, the streaming media services market was valued at USD 11.0 billion. Based on Fact MR analysis, demand for streaming media services is estimated to grow to USD 12.9 billion in 2026 and USD 61.1 billion by 2036. FMR projects a CAGR of 16.8% during the forecast period.

The absolute dollar growth from 2026 to 2036 is USD 48.2 billion. This level of expansion reflects a structural shift in digital entertainment distribution rather than incremental growth within traditional media channels. Streaming platforms deliver on demand video, music, and live content directly through internet connected devices, replacing conventional broadcast models in many regions. Growth is supported by rising smartphone penetration, broadband connectivity, and expanding subscription based digital content ecosystems. Market expansion remains influenced by high content production costs, licensing agreements for media distribution rights, and intense competition among streaming platform operators.

India leads with a projected CAGR of 20.9%, supported by rapid growth in mobile internet usage and expanding digital entertainment consumption across younger audiences. China follows with a CAGR of 18.8%, driven by strong domestic streaming platforms and large scale digital content distribution networks. Germany records a CAGR of 16.4%, reflecting steady adoption of subscription based streaming services across households. The United States shows the slowest growth at 15.8%, reflecting a mature streaming ecosystem where platform competition and subscriber saturation influence expansion. Mature digital media markets generate increasing replacement demand as viewers shift from traditional television subscriptions to streaming based content platforms.

The Streaming Media Services Market includes digital platforms that deliver video, audio, and multimedia content to users through internet based streaming technology. These services allow consumers to access entertainment, music, television programs, films, and live broadcasts without downloading files. Content is transmitted in real time from remote servers to connected devices such as smart televisions, computers, tablets, and smartphones.

America Movil 2025 Results: Revenue Grows as 5G, Fiber and Enterprise Services Drive Growth
sum: America Movil delivered strong fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 results, supported by rising service revenues, expanding 5G and fiber networks, and a sharp jump in net profit fueled by foreign exchange gains. The Latin American telecom giant outlined a disciplined capital strategy and signaled readiness for regional consolidation.

America Movil reported Q4 2025 revenue of Mex$244.9 billion, representing a 3.4 percent year-over-year increase. Service revenue grew at 5.3 percent, reflecting strong demand across mobile, broadband, and enterprise segments.

EBITDA reached Mex$94.9 billion, rising 4.2 percent year-over-year. The company maintained a strong EBITDA margin of 38.8 percent as earnings grew faster than revenue, highlighting operating efficiency and cost control initiatives.

Net profit surged to Mex$19.13 billion, up 350 percent compared with Q4 2024. The increase was largely driven by foreign exchange gains that cut financing costs by nearly half, significantly boosting bottom-line performance.
The company continued to emphasize financial discipline, targeting a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio between 1.3x and 1.5x while returning capital to shareholders.

Cadillac strengthens 2026 F1 entry with Tenneco technical deal and América Móvil backing
sum: The Cadillac Formula 1 Team has confirmed two strategically important partnerships as it accelerates preparations for its entry into the FIA Formula One World Championship in 2026, appointing Tenneco as an official technical partner and welcoming América Móvil as a major commercial partner.

The agreements significantly strengthen both the technical depth and commercial scale of Cadillac’s Formula 1 programme, which is being developed as a long-term, manufacturer-led operation aligned with the sport’s upcoming regulatory cycle.

Under a multi-year agreement, Tenneco will contribute its expertise across advanced powertrain systems, emissions technologies, ride performance solutions and materials engineering. The collaboration is expected to focus on performance-critical areas shaped by the 2026 regulations, including efficiency, thermal management, component durability and the application of advanced automotive technologies within a high-performance motorsport environment.

The partnership will play a key role in supporting Cadillac’s engineering roadmap as F1 introduces a new generation of hybrid power units, while also enabling technology transfer opportunities that may inform future road-car development.

In parallel, Cadillac has secured a partnership with América Móvil, one of Latin America’s largest telecommunications groups. The agreement sees América Móvil represented through its flagship brands Telcel, Infinitum, and Claro, which will feature across the Cadillac Formula 1 Team’s competitive, commercial and digital platforms.

The partnership delivers immediate regional reach and commercial momentum, particularly across Mexico and Latin America, markets that continue to show strong growth in F1 viewership and fan engagement. América Móvil brings extensive experience in global motorsport sponsorship, providing Cadillac with an established activation framework ahead of the team’s on-track debut.

Collectively, the announcements highlight Cadillac’s intent to build a fully integrated Formula One operation ahead of 2026, combining engineering capability with globally scaled commercial partnerships.

items.t: Cadillac land major Sergio Perez sponsor
sum: Cadillac has reaped the reward from its signing of Sergio Perez by landing one of the Mexican driver's long-term partners.
Perez has been heavily supported throughout his F1 career by a plethora of major Mexican brands, leading to América Movil opting to partner with F1's newest team.
The Mexican telecommunications giant will be represented by its familiar names - Telcel, Infinitum, and Claro - which will be on the cars and in the paddock.
Cadillac's global head of commercial strategy Tyler Epp said: “We are delighted to welcome América Móvil to the Cadillac Formula 1 Team at this exciting stage in our journey.

"Above all, we want to be a strong contributor to the sport, and having brands with a long history of Formula 1 participation will help us connect authentically with existing fans of Formula 1 while reaching ones in emerging markets."

Swayed by Perez signing for Cadillac, América Móvil chief marketing officer Marcela Velasco Cámara said: "When Sergio joined the Cadillac Formula 1 Team, we saw the scale of their ambition, and it was only natural for us to be part of their journey.
"Our partnership with the Cadillac Formula 1 Team reflects América Móvil’s vision of advancing world-class technology platforms that connect talent, speed, and innovation with millions of people.
